findings.body:
The new comment says chat-completions legs are `anthropic` and `codex`, with no-ops only on `claude-code`/`cursor`. That is wrong: `CodexProvider` subclasses `AgentRunnerProvider`, so complexity labeling is chat-completions-only (`anthropic`). With this config, the codex leg will log the agent-runner no-op warning and never apply `complexity:*`. Align the comment with `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` § provider support matrix (and the PR description, which currently repeats the same mistake).

```suggestion
          # PR complexity labeling — dogfood docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md
          # § `complexity-labels-enabled`. The model calls `set_pr_complexity`
          # and applies `complexity:low|medium|high`. Only the chat-completions
          # leg (`anthropic`) performs the assessment; agent-runner legs
          # (`claude-code`, `cursor`, `codex`) log a no-op warning by design.
          complexity-labels-enabled: true
          complexity-label-prefix: 'complexity:'
```

This header now points readers at `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` § "Recipe: run once when labelled `AIReview`…", but that section is still titled and written for `ready` / `no-ready-label`. Same drift in `AGENTS.md` ("label-gated on `ready`") and README links that treat this workflow as the reference implementation. Either keep the recipe title as `ready` here (consumer-facing example name) while only changing the repo's concrete label, or update the docs/AGENTS references in the same PR so maintainers are not sent to a non-existent section.

`label-gate` (and the matching scope bash / `empty_reason`) flip from `ready` to `AIReview`, but the PR title/summary only advertise complexity-label dogfooding, and the test plan still says “apply the `ready` label”. After merge, applying `ready` will no longer start self-review or arm the merge gate — a silent maintainer workflow break unless `AGENTS.md`, contributor docs, and any branch-protection/label habits are updated in lockstep. If the rename is intentional, call it out in the PR body and sync the docs; if not, drop the rename from this change.

summary:
Looks good on the intended complexity-label dogfood, but the PR also renames the self-review gate label and ships an incorrect provider note — address those before merge.

## Narrative

The `complexity-labels-enabled: true` + default `complexity-label-prefix: 'complexity:'` block is a reasonable Rule #10 dogfood of `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md`. Inputs match `action.yml`, permissions already include `pull-requests: write`, and the feature is best-effort / opt-in. No new secrets, subprocesses, or unpinned third-party actions.

Two problems sit next to that change:

1. **Wrong provider split in the new comment (and the PR description).** Only `anthropic` is chat-completions here. `codex` is an `AgentRunnerProvider` and will no-op complexity labeling with a WARNING, same as `claude-code` / `cursor`. The test plan’s “anthropic leg applies the label” expectation is fine; claiming codex does too is not.

2. **`ready` → `AIReview` is a large, mostly undocumented behavior change.** Scope matching, `label-gate`, `empty_reason` (`no-ready-label` → `no-gate-label`), gate `if:`, and operator-facing messages all move. Contributor docs still say this workflow is label-gated on `ready` (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` recipe title, README links). The PR title/test plan still talk about `ready`. After merge, maintainers who keep using `ready` will get skipped reviews and a skipped merge gate with no obvious signal in this PR’s summary.

Security/workflow posture of the YAML itself looks fine: no `${{ github.event.pull_request.* }}` shell interpolation, explicit `permissions`, `persist-credentials: false` unchanged.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
